method.title: Source-balanced Bradley–Terry preference models
method.description: Separate regularized logistic ranking models fit static and dynamic class preferences. Within each class and property, each publication gets equal total weight and its records share that weight. Every class pair gets equal fitting weight. Fixed L2 penalty 0.05 controls separation; it is not selected using held-out results.
method.probabilityMeaning: For classes A and B, the target is w·[P(A>B on strength)+0.5P(A=B)] + (1−w)·[P(A>B on fracture/failure resistance)+0.5P(A=B)]. The model probability approximates this randomly selected-axis preference. It is NOT the probability of exceeding B on BOTH axes. Fréchet bounds describe the joint preference allowed by the randomly tie-broken marginal comparisons; they are not strict two-axis dominance probabilities, and impose no independence assumption.
method.bootstrapNote: Source-block resampling measures literature sampling stability, not guaranteed rank confidence. Single-paper class axes cannot identify between-paper variation. Cross-products of source values and bootstrap replicates never increase the experimental sample count.
limitations: Higher strength and higher fracture/failure resistance are declared objectives, not a universal definition of better. Objective weights are user preferences.
Class populations can contain different alloys, processing states and test conditions between maps. Rank changes do not establish a same-material reversal or physical static-to-dynamic conversion.

Only original positive scalar experimental evidence with full-text review enters dynamic fitting. Estimated HEL, substituted coordinates, compilation summaries, range-only values and zero spall are excluded from ML; they remain in the atlas.
Tensile/compressive yield and toughness families have separate scenarios. J-integral values, tensile strength and Charpy energy never substitute for K or yield.
Temperature, loading rate, microstructure and publication are incompletely observed and confounded. There is no causal parameter-effect or out-of-class property-prediction claim.
A total-order model can compress tradeoffs and non-transitive preferences. Inspect separate axis preferences, method scenarios, fitting residuals and source-level held-out losses.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0; fracture/failure resistance has weight 1. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.272 for static-order transfer and 0.232 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 17 of 17 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.25; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.75. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.251 for static-order transfer and 0.237 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 17 of 17 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.5; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.5. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.237 for static-order transfer and 0.244 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 17 of 17 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.75; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.25. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.230 for static-order transfer and 0.253 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 17 of 17 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0; fracture/failure resistance has weight 1. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.99, dynamic 0.33; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.90, dynamic 0.14. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.521 for static-order transfer and 0.181 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 18 of 18 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.25; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.75. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.86, dynamic 0.28; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.81, dynamic 0.24. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.438 for static-order transfer and 0.217 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 18 of 18 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.5; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.5. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.65, dynamic 0.22; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.77, dynamic 0.35. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.333 for static-order transfer and 0.220 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 18 of 18 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.75; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.25. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is 0.333 and Spearman rho is 0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.214 for static-order transfer and 0.189 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 18 of 18 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 1; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is 1.000 and Spearman rho is 1.000. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.089 for static-order transfer and 0.127 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 18 of 18 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

scenarios.label: All reported K families · mixed-method sensitivity
scenarios.note: Independent measured marginal properties support each class; the axes need not come from the same material, test or paper. No joint samples are manufactured. Mixed K methods make this a confounded sensitivity analysis.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0; fracture/failure resistance has weight 1. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 4 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.667 and Spearman rho is -0.800. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.98, dynamic 0.31; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.86, dynamic 0.13; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.15, dynamic 0.77. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 4 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.477 for static-order transfer and 0.208 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 26 of 26 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.25; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.75. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 4 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.600. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.83, dynamic 0.25; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.79, dynamic 0.22; Metallic glasses vs Steels: static preference 0.16, dynamic 0.63; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.19, dynamic 0.66. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 4 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.404 for static-order transfer and 0.229 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 26 of 26 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.5; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.5. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 4 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.600. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Metallic glasses: static preference 0.59, dynamic 0.19; Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.78, dynamic 0.33; Metallic glasses vs Steels: static preference 0.37, dynamic 0.72; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.19, dynamic 0.56. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 4 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.319 for static-order transfer and 0.229 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 26 of 26 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.75; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.25. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 4 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is 0.667 and Spearman rho is 0.800. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.80, dynamic 0.45. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 4 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.227 for static-order transfer and 0.209 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 26 of 26 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

findings.title: A total ordering compresses some trade-offs
findings.text: At least one fitted preference differs from its direct weighted marginal comparison by more than 0.10. A Bradley–Terry score uses all class contests, so indirect comparisons and non-transitive trade-offs can move a pair away from its direct target. Inspect the empirical and per-axis comparisons before interpreting the fitted rank.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.text: Strength has weight 1; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 4 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is 1.000 and Spearman rho is 1.000. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 4 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is 1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.132 for static-order transfer and 0.171 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 26 of 26 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0; fracture/failure resistance has weight 1. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.247 for static-order transfer and 0.255 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 10 source holdouts are evaluable. validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.25; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.75. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: No class pair has opposite fitted directions separated from 0.5 by at least 0.05 in both maps at this objective weight. This does not establish equivalence of the regimes.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.257 for static-order transfer and 0.258 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 10 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.75; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.25. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Steels: static preference 0.59, dynamic 0.39. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.280 for static-order transfer and 0.269 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 10 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 1; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Too few classes for rank-correlation inference
findings.text: Only 2 comparable classes (or tied scores) are available. Rank-correlation coefficients are withheld; pairwise preferences and source counts remain visible.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Steels: static preference 0.62, dynamic 0.40. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.292 for static-order transfer and 0.277 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 10 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

scenarios.label: Measured condition pairs · mixed K sensitivity
scenarios.note: Only measured condition pairs support each map; they are not matched between regimes. Mixed K methods make this a confounded sensitivity analysis.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0; fracture/failure resistance has weight 1. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.93, dynamic 0.04; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.03, dynamic 0.94. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is -1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.25; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.75. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -0.333 and Spearman rho is -0.500. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.93, dynamic 0.08; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.06, dynamic 0.88. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is -1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.527 for static-order transfer and 0.163 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 11 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.5; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.5. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -1.000 and Spearman rho is -1.000. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.93, dynamic 0.14; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.09, dynamic 0.82. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is -1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.498 for static-order transfer and 0.197 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 11 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.

validation.note: Leave one dynamic publication out of BOTH regimes. Only classes with both admitted axes remaining in both training corpora are scored. Losses compare held-out dynamic marginal ordering with other training publications, macro-averaged by directed class pair and axis. These are correlated comparison diagnostics, not independent test counts or property predictions. Lower Brier/log loss is better; the no-ordering baseline is 0.25 / ln(2).

bootstrap.note: Whole publications are resampled jointly across both maps. Replicates missing any required class axis are omitted, never imputed. Ranges are 2.5–97.5% resampling stability ranges conditional on retained classes, not confidence guarantees for physical ranks. At least 32 complete replicates are required; single-source class ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Ordering is conditional on the chosen objectives
findings.text: Strength has weight 0.75; fracture/failure resistance has weight 0.25. Both properties are preferred higher. The two Bradley–Terry models summarize source-balanced within-property comparisons; this is a declared preference, not a universal material-quality score.

findings.title: Rank agreement
findings.text: 3 classes share all four admitted axes. Kendall tau-b is -1.000 and Spearman rho is -1.000. These compare literature class populations, not matched materials.

findings.title: Candidate changes in ordering
findings.text: Light alloys vs Pure metals: static preference 0.93, dynamic 0.20; Light alloys vs Steels: static preference 0.64, dynamic 0.43; Pure metals vs Steels: static preference 0.12, dynamic 0.76. These are sampling- and method-dependent candidates, not evidence that a matched material changes intrinsic performance.

findings.title: Mixed toughness methods confound this sensitivity view
findings.text: This deliberately broader scenario pools reported notched K, provisional KQ and other K families. Method mix and material composition differ by class. Its reversals remain candidates even if resampling is stable; check the separate method scenarios before interpreting them.

findings.title: Between-paper uncertainty is missing for some classes
findings.text: At least one of the four class axes has only one supporting paper. Its between-publication uncertainty cannot be learned by repeating that paper, so class rank ranges and affected pairwise ranges are withheld.

findings.title: Strength and fracture resistance tell different parts of the story
findings.text: Across 3 class medians, yield-to-HEL Kendall tau-b is -1.000, while K-to-spall tau-b is -0.333. These are source-balanced marginal medians from different populations. Agreement on strength does not require agreement on fracture/failure resistance.

findings.title: Does the static ordering carry into a held-out dynamic paper?
findings.text: Expected Brier loss is 0.478 for static-order transfer and 0.231 for the dynamic-trained model; 0.250 is the no-ordering baseline (lower is better). 10 of 11 source holdouts are evaluable. These point diagnostics have no significance test or independent-comparison claim; a lower loss alone does not establish generalization to a new material class.
